title: Two Pointer
description: Use when sorted array or string allows converging from both ends
groups: Pattern 1: Opposite-Direction Pointers (converge from both ends)
Pattern 2: Same-Direction Pointers (slow / fast, in-place overwrite)
Pattern 3: Fast & Slow Pointers on Linked Lists
Pattern 4: Sliding Window (a two-pointer variant with a shrinking/expanding window)

title: Sliding Window
description: Use when finding optimal contiguous subarray/substring

title: Binary Search
description: Use when you can define a monotonic predicate over a search space
groups: 1. Classic Binary Search on a Sorted Array
2. Binary Search on Rotated Sorted Array
4. Binary Search on the Answer — Minimize the Maximum
5. Binary Search on the Answer — Maximize the Minimum
7. Binary Search Across Two Sorted Structures / Kth Element
8. Binary Search on Real-Valued / Root-Finding Problems

title: Backtracking
description: Use when exploring all possibilities with choose/explore/unchoose

title: Greedy
description: Use when locally optimal choices lead to a globally optimal solution
groups: 1. Interval Scheduling — Sort by End Time
2. Interval Merging — Sort by Start Time

title: Bit Manipulation
description: Use when operations on individual bits can simplify the solution
groups: Group 2: XOR Properties — Finding Unique/Missing Elements
Group 6: Advanced XOR — Trie on Bits

title: Graph
description: Use when modeling relationships, paths, or connectivity between entities
groups: A. Grid Traversal (DFS/BFS Flood Fill & Connected Components)
C. Topological Sort (DAG Ordering & Cycle Detection)
E. Dijkstra's Algorithm (Weighted Shortest Path, Non-negative Weights)
F. Bellman-Ford (Shortest Path with Constraints / Negative Weights)

title: Dynamic Programming
description: Use when optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems exist
